The current and frequency points are driven through a 50-turn coil (calibrator current x 50 = the reading shown); their Uncertainty is that of the 5500A/COIL scope lines at the effective current where the lines cover it (frequency: the calibrator's frequency uncertainty).
source.note: Table 4 (48 rows: temperature 4, AC volts 5, DC volts 5, ohms 9, capacitance 3, frequency 3, AC amps 15, DC amps 4; printed pp. 13-14 of the 323 / 324 / 325 Calibration Manual). The table has no step numbers: steps are numbered in table order (4-1 .. 4-48). One family spec: the X columns decide the models (323: 16 points, 324: 24, 325: 30). Table 3 (printed p. 8) names a calibrator with 4.5 digit resolution (Fluke 5520A recommended; the program drives a Fluke 5522A, 5520A or 5560A, or you set the calibrator by hand) and the 5500A/COIL (50 turns). The AC / DC amps rows are driven through the 50-turn coil: the Calibrator Output is the current the calibrator drives and the meter reads 50 x that (the limits are meter readings). The three Frequency rows (325) are ASSIGNED TO THE COIL (0.2 A through the coil = 10 A in the jaw): the manual lists them with the lead tests but a NORMAL output cannot make an amps value (UNVERIFIED inference). The meter has no remote interface: you type the display reading. Limits are as printed (nothing is changed); the 30K ohm row is a printed misprint (34.65 KΩ / 30.35 Ω) and is used as 29.65 kΩ / 30.35 kΩ, visibly flagged. The manual prints no ranges, resolutions or accuracy figures. The functional tests (display, firmware, backlight, buttons; printed pp. 9-10) and the calibration ADJUSTMENT (printed pp. 15-) are not part of this procedure.

COIL_AUX.title: Change the cables: 50-turn coil on the calibrator low-current output
COIL_AUX.summary: Calibrator low-current output (5522A / 5520A AUX HI / AUX LO; 5560A VI AUX / OUTPUT LO) -> 50-turn coil (5500A/COIL) -> the meter jaw closed around the coil. No test leads in the meter jacks.
steps: Meter dial
Turn the meter dial to OFF before you move any lead.
Test leads
REMOVE the test leads from the VΩ and COM jacks while the current is measured with the jaw (general practice; the Calibration Manual does not say).
Standby
The calibrator is put in STANDBY before you rewire (in manual-calibrator mode, put it in STANDBY yourself).
Coil

The wired coil is 50 turns (Table 3, printed p. 8: 5500A/COIL). Connect its two ends to the calibrator current output and ground (Figure 5): Fluke 5522A / 5520A AUX HI and AUX LO; Fluke 5560A VI AUX (HI) and OUTPUT LO. Use plugs rated for the current.
Jaw
Close the jaw around the coil, fully closed, the coil centred in the opening, the coil leads kept away from the meter body. The meter then reads 50 x the calibrator current (0.2 A reads 10 A).
LCOMP
Fluke 5522A / 5520A: for the AC points switch inductive-load compensation (LCOMP) ON at the calibrator front panel when the coil needs it. The program does not set it: UNVERIFIED for this coil.
Check
Compare your connections with the diagram, then continue.
COIL_AUX.caution: This point drives current through a coil. Keep the calibrator in STANDBY whenever you touch the coil or leads.

COIL_20A.title: Change the cables: 50-turn coil on the calibrator high-current output
COIL_20A.summary: Calibrator high-current output (5522A / 5520A 20 A / AUX LO; 5560A 30A / OUTPUT LO) -> 50-turn coil (5500A/COIL) -> the meter jaw closed around the coil. No test leads in the meter jacks.
steps: Meter dial
Turn the meter dial to OFF before you move any lead.
Test leads
REMOVE the test leads from the VΩ and COM jacks while the current is measured with the jaw (general practice; the Calibration Manual does not say).
Standby
The calibrator is put in STANDBY before you rewire (in manual-calibrator mode, put it in STANDBY yourself).
Coil

Move the two ends of the 50-turn coil to the calibrator high-current terminals: Fluke 5522A / 5520A 20 A and AUX LO; Fluke 5560A 30A and OUTPUT LO. The coil, plugs and leads must carry up to 7.8 A (4.2 A and 7.8 A on the 323, 6 A on the 324 and 325).
Jaw
The jaw stays closed around the coil (centred, fully closed, leads away from the meter body). The meter reads 50 x the calibrator current: 4.2 A reads 210 A, 6 A reads 300 A, 7.8 A reads 390 A.
LCOMP
Fluke 5522A / 5520A: AC points with LCOMP ON when the coil needs it (not set by the program; UNVERIFIED for this coil).
Check
Compare your connections with the diagram, then continue.
COIL_20A.caution: Up to 7.8 A flows in the coil. Keep the calibrator in STANDBY whenever you touch the coil or leads; check that the coil and leads are not warm after a long run (duty cycle not confirmed for this coil: UNVERIFIED).

TEMP.title: Change the cables: temperature (thermocouple simulation)
TEMP.summary: Calibrator thermocouple output (TC) -> the meter temperature input (see the Users Manual for the meter: the Calibration Manual does not describe the temperature connection).
steps: Meter dial
Turn the meter dial to OFF before you move any lead, then to the temperature function.
Standby
The calibrator is put in STANDBY before you rewire (in manual-calibrator mode, put it in STANDBY yourself).
Connection

Connect the calibrator thermocouple (TC) output to the meter temperature input with the correct thermocouple cable and adapter for the meter (K-type assumed, UNVERIFIED). Figure 4 of the Calibration Manual shows the NORMAL output and ground on the meter VΩ and COM jacks for the group of tests that includes temperature; if your meter takes the thermocouple there, use that connection instead.
Soak
Let the cable and meter settle to room temperature before the first temperature point.
Check
Compare your connections with the diagram, then continue.
TEMP.caution: The output is a simulated thermocouple signal (millivolts). Keep the calibrator in STANDBY while you connect the leads.
